# implicit-sdf.library: ExponentialSmoothUnionDistance

**Status:** Supported (tier `geometry`). In a shipping tier; the lint, type-check, and code-generation gates cover it. No release promises its signature yet.

## Summary

> The exponential smooth minimum of two distances. Unlike the polynomial
> SmoothUnionDistance this operator is ASSOCIATIVE: blending three or more shapes
> gives the same result in any order, where the polynomial form's answer depends
> on how the operands were parenthesized. That is what it buys for the price of
> two exponentials and a logarithm. A lower bound, like the polynomial form:
> its operand weights sum to one. Precondition: blendRadius is positive.
> (https://iquilezles.org/articles/smin/)

## Signature

```plato
ExponentialSmoothUnionDistance(a: Number, b: Number, blendRadius: Number): Number
```

## Laws

These are declared laws. Whether each one passes is recorded by the law runner ([stdlib/VERIFICATION.md](../../../../../stdlib/VERIFICATION.md)), not by this page.

### Law_ExponentialSmoothUnionIsAssociative

[stdlib/tests/implicit-sdf.laws.plato, line 234](../../../../../stdlib/tests/implicit-sdf.laws.plato#L234)

```plato
// The exponential smooth minimum is ASSOCIATIVE, which is the property that
// distinguishes it from the polynomial form: combining three distances gives the
// same answer whichever pair is blended first. The polynomial SmoothUnionDistance
// does NOT satisfy this, which is why no matching law exists for it.
Law_ExponentialSmoothUnionIsAssociative(a: Number, b: Number, c: Number, blendRadius: Number): Boolean
    => blendRadius <= 0.0
    || ExponentialSmoothUnionDistance(ExponentialSmoothUnionDistance(a, b, blendRadius), c, blendRadius)
        .LawEq(ExponentialSmoothUnionDistance(a, ExponentialSmoothUnionDistance(b, c, blendRadius), blendRadius));
```

### Law_ExponentialSmoothUnionIsNoGreaterThanUnion

[stdlib/tests/implicit-sdf.laws.plato, line 241](../../../../../stdlib/tests/implicit-sdf.laws.plato#L241)

```plato
// Exponential smoothing, like the polynomial form, never exceeds the sharp
// minimum it approximates.
Law_ExponentialSmoothUnionIsNoGreaterThanUnion(a: Number, b: Number, blendRadius: Number): Boolean
    => blendRadius <= 0.0
    || ExponentialSmoothUnionDistance(a, b, blendRadius) <= UnionDistance(a, b) + 1e-4;
```

### Line 728

**Source:** [stdlib/geometry/implicit-sdf.library.plato, line 728](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/implicit-sdf.library.plato#L728).

```plato

    // The exponential smooth minimum of two distances. Unlike the polynomial
    // SmoothUnionDistance this operator is ASSOCIATIVE: blending three or more shapes
    // gives the same result in any order, where the polynomial form's answer depends
    // on how the operands were parenthesized. That is what it buys for the price of
    // two exponentials and a logarithm. A lower bound, like the polynomial form:
    // its operand weights sum to one. Precondition: blendRadius is positive.
    // (https://iquilezles.org/articles/smin/)
    ExponentialSmoothUnionDistance(a: Number, b: Number, blendRadius: Number): Number
        => ((a.Negative / blendRadius).Exp + (b.Negative / blendRadius).Exp).NaturalLog
           * blendRadius.Negative;
```
